learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: Linear algebra, geometry, differential geometry, differential and integral calculus, differential and partial differential equations, numerical methods and numerical algorithms.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Engineering

Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in the different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Ability to know, understand and use the principles of differential calculus in several variables.

assessment_rules: Progressive assessment combines solved exercises (20%), oral presentations (20%), and a written exam (60%). A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for oral presentations. Students failing progressive assessment may take a global written exam worth 100%, requiring a minimum grade of 5 out of 10. A second resit opportunity is available with another 100% written exam if the previous attempts fail.
